title: Framework Hosts Wasm Storybook Stories
description: Create .storybook/stories/framework/hosts/ (scope id "framework/hosts", titlePrefix "🛠️framework🔌️hosts", already registered in .storybook/scopes.ts) covering the framework renderer hosts backed by prebuilt Rust/WASM engines: NodeGraphHost.stories.tsx (incl. flow-graph variant via isFlowGraphScene/fixtureJson + flow/core wasm), TextEditorHost.stories.tsx, Paint2dHost.stories.tsx, TiledMapHost.stories.tsx, WorldTerrainLayer.stories.tsx (wrapped in an r3f Canvas), World3dHost.stories.tsx. Verify each engine's prebuilt pkg/*.wasm artifact exists before storying it (never trigger a cargo build). Add single-flight loader functions to WASM_LOADERS in .storybook/preview.tsx for node-graph/editor/paint-2d/tiled-map/terrain/flow, gated via parameters.wasm. A separate concurrent workstream is writing the non-wasm hosts (TableHost/BlockListHost/GraphTimelineHost/IconRenderHost/InkCanvasHost/Canvas2dHost/UiInterpreter) in the same directory — do not touch those filenames. Verify the scope boots via bun ./📜️script.ts dev storybook framework/hosts and add a playwright spec (.storybook/framework-hosts-wasm.spec.ts) iterating the new story ids for a 200 status / no significant console errors. Part of the parallel workforce populating the composable root Storybook (parent ticket FEATURE-COMPLETE-COMPOSABLE-STORYBOOK-COVERING-THE-MONOREPO).
summary:
Added 6 story files to .storybook/stories/framework/hosts/ (already-registered scope, titlePrefix "🛠️framework🔌️hosts"), covering every framework renderer host backed by a prebuilt Rust/WASM engine: NodeGraphHost.stories.tsx (MediaGraph = default WasmGraphSurface/GraphSession variant, FlowGraph = FlowGraphCanvasHost/FlowSession variant via isFlowGraphScene/fixtureJson routing), TextEditorHost.stories.tsx (EditorSession), Paint2dHost.stories.tsx (RasterSession, composite + navigator views), TiledMapHost.stories.tsx (MapSession, vector + image render modes), WorldTerrainLayer.stories.tsx (TerrainSession, wrapped in a standalone @react-three/fiber Canvas since it's normally mounted inside World3dHost's own WorldCanvas), World3dHost.stories.tsx (MinimalViewport needs no wasm at all — pure r3f/@semio-tech/infinite-world-r3f — TerrainViewport sets terrainJson so it mounts WorldTerrainLayer against the real TerrainSession engine). 15 story/docs entries total (12 stories + 3 autodocs pages; World3dHost/WorldTerrainLayer opted out of autodocs via tags: ["!autodocs"] since their r3f render loops are nondeterministic to re-render as static docs snapshots).

Verified every engine's prebuilt pkg/*.wasm artifact actually exists on disk before storying it (node-graph, editor, paint-2d, tiled-map, terrain, flow/core) — never triggered a cargo build. Added 6 single-flight loader functions to WASM_LOADERS in .storybook/preview.tsx (node-graph/editor/paint-2d/tiled-map/terrain/flow), generalized behind a small `singleFlightWasmInit` helper using the same bare `@semio-tech/framework-surface-*-rs/pkg/*.js` specifiers the framework renderer itself uses internally (bun-symlinked workspace packages, no scope alias needed — verified via `node_modules/@semio-tech/*` symlinks), following the existing `compose` entry's dynamic-import + init + single-flight-cache pattern. Confirmed World3dHost needs no wasm of its own (pure r3f + @semio-tech/infinite-world-r3f) by reading its actual render body; confirmed WorldTerrainLayer's real prop signature (terrainJson/cameraPosition/cameraTarget) by reading its source directly rather than assuming. All scene JSON fixtures were cross-checked against the real TypeScript scene types in framework/core/js/index.ts and, for the flow fixture, against the actual Rust FlowFixture/Widget/SynapseSpec structs in flow/core/rs/lib.rs (not guessed).

Added .storybook/framework-hosts-wasm.spec.ts (new playwright spec, modeled on puzzle-2d.spec.ts/coda-trees.spec.ts): one test per story id (12 tests) asserting clean boot (no page/console errors beyond benign intentional-404 tile/DEM fetches) plus a host-specific marker per file.

Verified the scope boots via `bun ./📜️script.ts dev storybook framework/hosts`: index.json enumerates all 15 expected entries under the correct titles with zero missing-story warnings across three separate clean boots, coexisting cleanly with the concurrent workstream's 24 non-wasm host entries (TableHost/BlockListHost/GraphTimelineHost/IconRenderHost/InkCanvasHost/Canvas2dHost/UiInterpreter) in the same directory with no filename collisions. Spot-checked iframe.html for all 12 story ids (2 per file) — all returned HTTP 200 with real Storybook iframe HTML (storybook-root present, no "Couldn't find story" text). The environment was under severe, unrelated concurrent-session resource contention during verification (load average briefly 20-55, free memory in the tens of MB, one dev process observed in uninterruptible-sleep state) caused by ~9 other agents' simultaneous storybook/dev processes on this shared repo — this made early requests time out repeatedly (matches the sibling STYLING-SCOPE-STORYBOOK-STORIES ticket's same finding); resolved by restarting on a freshly-confirmed-free port and re-verifying end to end once contention eased, rather than concluding the stories were broken. All temporary server processes were torn down (ports 6047/6048 confirmed free) before closing.

Found but did NOT touch (pre-existing, out of scope, affects every non-"compose" Storybook scope): .storybook/preview.tsx's existing `WASM_LOADERS.compose` entry imports `@semio-tech/compose-rs-wasm` via `.storybook/compose/algorithm/kit-store/index.tsx`, whose alias is only registered for the "compose"/"compose/ui"/"compose/algorithm" scopes. When any OTHER scope (including framework/hosts, and presumably framework/os, styling, etc.) boots, Vite's dependency scanner fails to resolve it and logs "Failed to run dependency scan. Skipping dependency pre-bundling" — this appears to materially degrade first-load performance for every non-compose scope since large deps (e.g. three.js/@react-three/fiber for this scope) never get pre-bundled. Worth a follow-up ticket for whoever owns preview.tsx/WASM_LOADERS.
